title: Sell Mineral Rights in Lockwood, MT
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Lockwood, MT
metaDescription: Lockwood's oil-storage terminals and rail yards move crude, they don't produce it. I buy Yellowstone County mineral interests near Lockwood based on real records.
heroLead: Lockwood is full of tank farms and rail spurs moving other people's crude around — the minerals underneath it are a separate question entirely.
intro: Lockwood sits right up against Billings, and between the rail yards and the storage terminals it looks, to someone driving through, like an oil town. It isn't, in the sense that matters for a mineral owner — the infrastructure here is midstream, moving crude that was produced somewhere else, mostly the Bakken and Canadian fields, through to the Laurel refinery and beyond. If you hold minerals under a Lockwood-area parcel, I evaluate them on their own drilling and lease history, not on what's visibly running through the pipeyards nearby.

I make this distinction early with every Lockwood call because it saves everyone time. The infrastructure is real and it's substantial, but it tells you almost nothing about what's under the specific parcel your family owns.

sections.heading: Industrial surface, quiet mineral estate
paragraphs: A lot of the land around Lockwood has been sold or leased for industrial and commercial use over the past few decades, and in a fair number of those transactions the mineral rights were reserved separately rather than conveyed with the surface. If your family held onto minerals when a parcel here changed hands for industrial development, that reservation is still worth confirming even if there's no drilling nearby.

sections.heading: What I check before making an offer
paragraphs: I pull the recorded deed chain through the Yellowstone County Clerk and Recorder, check for any lease of record, and look at whether any operator has permitted activity nearby in recent years. Lockwood-area interests are usually valued on potential and location rather than current production, and I'm straightforward about that up front.

faqs.question: Do the storage terminals near Lockwood mean there's oil production there?
faqs.answer: No. That's midstream infrastructure moving crude produced elsewhere, mainly the Bakken and Canadian fields, through to the Laurel refinery. It doesn't reflect drilling on the ground itself.

faqs.question: My family reserved minerals when we sold land near Lockwood for development — can you still buy that?
faqs.answer: Yes. Reserved mineral interests on developed or industrial-use surface are common here and I buy them, confirmed through the recorded deed chain.

faqs.question: Is there any current leasing activity around Lockwood?
faqs.answer: Limited, but I check the status on your specific parcel before quoting rather than assuming based on the area generally.

faqs.question: Who do you check ownership with for a Lockwood parcel?
faqs.answer: The Yellowstone County Clerk and Recorder in Billings. I pull the record myself rather than relying on family memory of how the land was sold.
